layers.note: Forms dense stands at the edges of ponds, lakes, marshes and ditches.

moisture.note: Shallow standing water and saturated shores.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Flat ground at the water's edge.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −20 °C, gone by −30 °C, up to about 22 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 12 to 32 °C; gone below 9 °C, where summers are too short, and above 36 °C.

degree_days_0.note: Across its range, about 1,600 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,000.

degree_days_5.note: Across its range, about 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400.

moisture_index.note: It grows where the ground stays wet whatever the climate's moisture index, so only the driest climates (below about 0.1) rule it out; the site's own moisture places it.

summer_rain.note: No limit: it grows under summer-dry and summer-wet climates alike.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Broadleaf cattail is nearly cosmopolitan in marshes, from the subarctic to the tropics (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
